title: Bilinear magnon--exciton coupling in biased ferromagnetic electron--hole bilayers
abstract: Two-dimensional magnetic semiconductors provide a unique platform where strong magnon--exciton interactions can be realized. Owing to the intrinsic energy mismatch between excitons and magnons, however, these interactions are typically between the exciton density and magnons. We propose biased ferromagnetic electron--hole bilayers, where the exciton energy gap can be lowered with the voltage bias, as a platform in which excitons and magnons can instead couple resonantly. Starting from the microscopic exchange interactions between electrons and localized magnetic moments, we demonstrate the linear hybridization of magnons and spin-flip excitons in this regime. As the exciton energy is lowered further, a magnon--exciton Bose--Einstein condensate is formed. We show that this condensate is further modified by an attractive magnon--exciton density--density interaction, which we derive microscopically. We study the condensate's collective modes and demonstrate their hybridization with the magnons, providing an alternative detection mechanism for the formation of exciton condensates.
summary: This work theoretically investigates the resonant coupling between excitons and magnons in a biased ferromagnetic bilayer. By tuning the exciton energy, the system can achieve a bilinear coupling regime, leading to the formation of a magnon-exciton Bose-Einstein condensate. The study predicts observable spectral signatures of this hybridization.
main_problem: To study the resonant coupling between excitons and magnons in a biased ferromagnetic electron-hole bilayer, moving beyond simple density-magnon coupling.
main_result: The paper demonstrates bilinear magnon-exciton coupling, leading to hybridization of collective modes and the potential formation of a magnon-exciton Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC).
method: The analysis uses a microscopic derivation starting from exchange interactions, employing Green's functions and path integral formalism to derive coupled Gross-Pitaevskii equations.
model_or_system: The system is a biased ferromagnetic electron-hole bilayer, modeled by Hamiltonians including magnon, electron, and coupling terms. The coupling is tuned by a voltage bias to allow resonant interaction.
key_observables: Spectral density (measured via Brillouin light scattering/magneto-Raman), condensate densities ($n_X, n_a, n_o$), and the hybridization gap.
important_parameters: Voltage bias ($V$) tuning the exciton energy gap to the meV range; coupling strengths ($J_{\alpha eta}, \Gamma_0$).
main_assumptions: Approximations include the on-shell approximation and treating the system near homogeneous, time-independent condensate states to linearize fluctuations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the avoided crossing of energy spectra as the bias voltage is varied, confirming hybridization, and show the spectral density confirming this coupling in the condensed phase.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the full Hamiltonian and deriving the coupled action, to solving the resulting coupled Gross-Pitaevskii equations, and finally analyzing the resulting excitation spectrum via Bogoliubov theory.
why_interesting: The study of coupled bosonic systems (excitons and magnons) undergoing BEC formation and hybridization is highly relevant to understanding interacting quantum materials and collective excitations in condensed matter.
